title: Temporal Anomaly Hypothesis Framework and Dashboard Kit
author: Priya Rao
content:
Overview:

This page defines the Temporal Anomaly Hypothesis Framework (TAHF) and provides a reusable dashboard + alerting kit for investigating short- and medium-duration anomalies in platform telemetry (tokens/sec, tail latency, cache miss ratio, model swap rate, cost-per-token). The goal is to move operator investigation from ad-hoc firefighting to hypothesis-driven triage: formulate a small number of falsifiable hypotheses, run fast experiments/queries, and converge to mitigation actions within the first 30 minutes of an incident.

Motivation:

- Platform signals are high-cardinality and noisy; naive alerting produces noisy pages and long mean-time-to-detect/repair.
- Operators need a concise, repeatable workflow when faced with temporal anomalies (spikes, regressions, step-changes, slow-drifts).
- Provide a dashboard and query kit that supports quick A/B-style hypothesis checks and produces machine-readable evidence for postmortems.

Definitions and scope:

- Temporal anomaly: any unexpected deviation from baseline across a time window (seconds to hours). Examples: token request bursts, sudden tail-latency regressions, cache contention events.
- Baseline: rolling 7-day median + IQR by tenant-class (free/paid/enterprise) or by model-shard for internal services.
- Hypothesis: short declarative statement of a potential root/cause and a measurable prediction (e.g., "Spike is due to tenant X sending batched prefix requests; we expect per-tenant token rate to explain >60% of total delta").

High-level workflow (operator-facing):

1) Ingest alert and open the TAHF dashboard for the impacted region.
2) Immediately capture the top 3 candidate hypotheses using the template below.
3) Run the baseline checks (quick queries, widget correlation) to falsify at least one hypothesis within 10 minutes.
4) If none falsified, escalate to secondary investigator and enable targeted mitigations (rate-limits, temporary routing to variant model) within 20 minutes.
5) Log the final hypothesis and actions to the incident ticket and mark for postmortem input.

Hypothesis template (use in initial triage):

- Hypothesis ID: H1
- Statement: one-sentence cause hypothesis.
- Prediction: measurable numeric expectation and window (e.g., tenant X increase explains >= 60% of token delta in last 5m).
- Required queries/widgets: list of 2-4 metrics/queries to confirm/falsify.
- Confidence & next action: low/medium/high and immediate mitigation plan if confirmed.

Dashboard kit (widgets and recommended layout):

Top row - Incident snapshot (single-row summary widgets):
- Global delta sparkline (tokens/sec) vs 7d median (1m, 5m, 15m windows).
- Tail latency 99.9th percentile (ms) and delta percentage.
- Active model swaps/min and model-variant bleeding rate.
- Incidence score: weighted sum of token surge + latency surge + error rate (configurable weight table below).

Second row - Cardinated breakdowns (drill-down panels):
- By tenant class: tokens/sec and delta, top 10 tenants contributing to delta.
- By model-shard: requests/sec, cache-miss-rate, avg-kv-cache-evictions/min.
- By region/edge node: tail latency heatmap (per-az breakdown).

Third row - Hypothesis probes (quick queries to run):
- Tenants: per-tenant contribution query (example PromQL below).
- Prefetch/KV cache: eviction rate and prefix-cache-hit-rate.
- Batching: average batch size distribution and sudden shifts.
- Downstream services: third-party model-host latency and drop rates.

Operator alert rules (recommended starting set):

Rule 1: Temporal surge alert (short-window)
- Trigger: tokens/sec > baseline + 5 * IQR for 3 consecutive 1m buckets
- Severity: P2
- Operator action: open TAHF dashboard, capture hypotheses H1-H3, run per-tenant contribution query

Rule 2: Tail latency burst
- Trigger: p99.9 latency > 2x baseline for 3m and error-rate increase > 0.5%
- Severity: P1
- Operator action: verify model swaps, check CPU/GPU utilization on target pool, consider model-variant fallback

Rule 3: KV cache thundering
- Trigger: prefix-cache-eviction-rate > 250 evictions/min and cache-hit-rate drop > 20%
- Severity: P2
- Operator action: confirm eviction storms, enable per-tenant kv-cache backoff, assess prefix hotness

Example queries (Prometheus/Traces/SQL snippets):

- Per-tenant token contribution (PromQL):
  sum(rate(redwood_requests_tokens_total{job="runtime",region="us-west-2"}[1m])) by (tenant_id)
  --> sort_desc and show top 20, compare to global delta

- Cache miss ratio (PromQL):
  sum(rate(kv_cache_miss_total[1m])) / sum(rate(kv_cache_lookup_total[1m])) by (model_shard)

- Average batch size distribution (SQL over telemetry store):
  SELECT bin_size, count(*) AS requests FROM batch_events WHERE ts > now() - interval '10 minutes' GROUP BY bin_size ORDER BY bin_size DESC LIMIT 50;

Dashboard widget spec (text table):

- Widget: "Top contributing tenants" | Type: table | Query: per-tenant token contribution | Columns: rank, tenant_id, tokens_1m, delta_vs_baseline | Refresh: 30s | Owner: platform-telemetry
- Widget: "Model shard heatmap" | Type: heatmap | Query: p99 latency by shard, region | Color scale: linear | Owner: serving-runtime
- Widget: "Hypothesis checklist" | Type: text/checkbox | Content: three hypothesis entries with links to quick queries | Owner: platform-oncall

Config and thresholds (operator-tunable):

- Baseline window: 7 days (default)
- Short-window anomaly sensitivity: IQR multiplier (default 5)
- Hypothesis check deadline: 10 minutes from alert open
- Escalation deadline: 20 minutes

Ownership and contacts:

- Dashboard owner: platform-observability (pager: #oncall-platform-observability)
- Primary incident owner for temporal anomalies: platform-operator-runbook (oncall rotation)
- Model-fallback owner: eng-serving-runtime (separate escalation)

Operator runbook (triage checklist) - execute in order:

1) Confirm alert validity:
   - Check for recent configuration changes (deploys, kernel switches) in the last 30 minutes. Query: deploy_events{service=~"runtime|allocator"} and correlate.
2) Snapshot evidence (first 5 minutes):
   - Save top-20 per-tenant token list, p99.9 latencies by shard, and active model swap count. Attach to ticket.
3) Run hypothesis probes (10 minutes):
   - H1: Tenant-driven surge? Run per-tenant token contribution and look for a top tenant explaining >60% delta. If yes, apply tenant soft-rate-limit and monitor.
   - H2: Model-variant regression? Verify model-variant BLEED and run comparison queries across variants. If confirmed, route to fallback variant.
   - H3: Cache storm / prefetch hotness? Inspect prefix-cache-eviction-rate and batch-size distribution. If confirmed, enable conservative prefetch backoff.
4) Apply minimal blast-radius mitigation first (15 minutes):
   - Prefer targeted tenant limits, model-variant routing, or temporary regional throttling over global changes.
5) Escalate to SRE/Serving Runtime if mitigation not effective within 20 minutes.

Post-incident artifacts (what to attach to ticket):

- Hypotheses tried and outcomes (use the template).
- Saved dashboard snapshot urls and raw query outputs.
- Operator play-by-play timestamps (actions taken and times).
- Suggested follow-ups for retrofit automation or alert tuning.

Retrospective guidance (to be included in postmortem):

- Label incident with dominant signal (tokens/latency/cache/other).
- Evaluate whether the IQR multiplier or baseline window needs tuning for this tenant-class.
- Capture additional instrumentation gaps and add instrumentation tickets (examples: per-prefix hotness metric, per-batch-id trace).
- If human mitigation was required repeatedly (>2 incidents in 30 days), create a small engineering project for automated mitigation.

Roadmap and next steps (quarterly):

- Q2 2026: Add per-prefix clustering on dashboard and automated candidate-tenant-suggestion for triage.
- Q3 2026: Integrate TAHF checklist into incident response UI and allow one-click mitigations (soft-rate-limit, variant-route).
- Q4 2026: Build a supervised classifier for anomaly type (tenant vs. model vs. cache) to reduce manual hypothesis count.

Appendix - Quick links and snippets:
